skeleton: a cosy nest holding three eggs (1 back-left, 2 back-right, 3 front), seen slightly from above: root at the nest's round bottom; nest on it carries the empty nest and, in front of everything, the front rim of twigs and ferns over the eggs' bottoms; each egg on its own bone at its bottom (it rocks there), its slot showing the egg whole or, broken, its lower shell (zigzag rim); a crack slot over it; the top cap on its own bone at its centre (it pops off); a baby Triceratops in each egg (baby bone at its base inside the shell, layered behind the lower shell so it sits inside it), hidden ('none') unless hatched: face bone with each eye and the mouth, two front paws over the rim, and a hat bone carrying the egg's cap when it lands on the baby's head; the cap swaps between the cap slot (on the egg) and the hat slot (on the head) on keys where they are in the same place. Every action starts and ends with the eggs whole; the hatched state lives in a pause. The nest itself only rocks as a bump would rock it.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a cosy dinosaur nest of twigs and fern fronds holding three big speckled eggs. Draw it as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate pieces laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every piece at the size it has in image 1 (if they do not all fit, draw them all a little smaller, at the same scale as each other).

Draw each piece on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no piece touching or overlapping another:
1. the nest EMPTY: the round nest of brown twigs and green fern fronds exactly as in image 1, seen slightly from above, but with no eggs in it: its hollow middle shows the soft inside of the nest, lined with twigs and fern, drawn whole, including everything the eggs hide in image 1.
2. the nest's front rim alone: only the near (front) part of the nest, the woven twigs of its front edge with the fern fronds that lie over the bottoms of the eggs in image 1, a wide curved band as it is in image 1; its top edge is the tips of those fronds, where they cross the eggs in image 1.
3. the back-left egg alone, whole: a big oval cream egg with pale-green speckles, tilted as it is in image 1, drawn whole, including its bottom that the nest and the other eggs hide in image 1.
4. the back-right egg alone, whole, the same way.
5. the front egg alone, whole, the same way.
6. the lower half of the egg of piece 3, broken open: the bottom half of the same eggshell, the same size, with the same speckles, its top edge a jagged zigzag broken rim running round the egg's middle; seen from the front, so the inside of the shell does not show.
7. the top cap of the egg of piece 3, broken off: the top of the same eggshell, its bottom edge the matching jagged zigzag, seen from the front.
8. the lower half of the egg of piece 4, broken open, the same way as piece 6.
9. the top cap of the egg of piece 4, the same way as piece 7.
10. the lower half of the egg of piece 5, broken open, the same way as piece 6.
11. the top cap of the egg of piece 5, the same way as piece 7.
12. a crack alone, as it would look on the egg of piece 5 when it starts to hatch: one jagged zigzag crack line running across the egg's middle from side to side, with two or three short little branches, drawn in the same dark brown line as the eggs' outline, all its lines joined in one piece, as wide as the egg, with no egg behind it.

Every piece is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another piece, with its edges clean and smooth. It is an object, not a character: no face, no eyes, no mouth, no animal. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the pieces beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows, no ground, no grass, no flying bits of shell, crumbs or sparkles. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a cosy dinosaur nest holding three big speckled eggs; image 2 shows that nest and its eggs cut into puppet pieces. The babies in those eggs are Triceratops; their mother is a friendly cartoon Triceratops: warm orange skin with darker orange-red round spots, a cream chest and belly, a big round frill edged with little cream knobs, cream horns, big glossy dark brown eyes with a white sparkle, rosy pink cheeks, a small dark nostril on its rounded beak-like snout and a closed smile, soft fuzzy textured shading and a thin dark brown outline. Draw a newborn baby Triceratops hatching from one of these eggs, as cut-out paper puppet pieces on one sheet, in exactly the drawing style, texture and line of image 1, coloured like the mother.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no piece touching or overlapping another:
1. the baby's head and shoulders, as it peeks up out of an egg: a tiny cute hatchling of that mother, with a big round head, a small rounded frill behind it with little cream knobs on its edge, two small soft rounded nub horns over its eyes and a tiny nub on its nose, warm orange with darker orange-red spots like its mother, then a short neck and the top of its chest and shoulders, with a cream chest; facing the viewer, turned just slightly to the left, with a completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth, but keep the rosy cheeks and the small nostril. Below the shoulders the piece simply ends (the rest of the body is inside the egg): its bottom edge is a soft rounded end with no outline drawn across it. Size: its head is about as wide as one of the eggs in image 2, and the whole piece is about one and a half eggs tall.
2. the baby's left front foot (on the left of the picture): a tiny round orange foot with three little cream toes like its mother's, as it would rest on the broken rim of an eggshell, its upper end a soft rounded end with no outline drawn across it.
3. the baby's right front foot, the same, drawn for its own side.

The baby is happy and gentle, nothing scary: no teeth, no claws. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the pieces beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows, no eggshell, no nest, no ground. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a dinosaur nest with three eggs; image 2 shows the baby Triceratops that hatches from them, cut into puppet pieces, with a blank face. Draw the baby's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style and line as image 1, a friendly cartoon style, every piece at the size it has on the baby's head in image 2, so it fits the blank face there (a baby's eyes: big and round for its head).

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the baby's left eye (on the left of the picture):
1. open: a big glossy dark brown eye with a white sparkle and a thin dark lid line, the iris sitting slightly to the left (looking a little to the left).
2. the same eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
3. the same eye gently closed: a soft downward-curving line with two or three little lashes.
4. the same eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
Row 2, the baby's right eye (on the right of the picture), drawn for its own side, never a mirror of the left one, its iris also slightly to the left:
5. open, the same big glossy eye.
6. wide open and surprised.
7. gently closed.
8. closed in a happy smile.
Row 3, the mouth (a little beak-like snout's smile):
9. a small closed happy smile, a soft curved dark brown line.
10. open in a big happy laugh, the inside pink, no teeth.
11. open in a small round 'o'.
12. open in a big sleepy yawn, the inside pink, no teeth.

Nothing scary: no teeth. No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the nest of eggs is set down on the ground: it rocks gently on its round bottom and settles, the eggs snug inside.
the front egg rocks gently from side to side, as if something inside is stirring, then sits still.
all three eggs rock gently in the nest, one after another, as the babies inside stir, then sit still.
the front egg wobbles and little cracks zigzag across its shell.

pause.shows: the front egg cracked across its middle, about to hatch

animations.description: the front egg wobbles and cracks, its top pops off and a baby Triceratops pushes its head out, its eggshell cap landing on its head; it blinks and smiles.

pause.shows: a baby Triceratops peeking out of the broken front egg, its eggshell cap on its head, smiling

animations.description: one after another, all three eggs crack and a baby Triceratops pops its head out of each, eggshell caps on their heads, and they smile.

pause.shows: three baby Triceratops peeking out of their broken eggs in the nest, eggshell caps on their heads, smiling

animations.description: the front egg cracks and its top lifts like a lid: a baby Triceratops peeks out underneath, looks this way and that, then ducks back inside.

pause.shows: a baby Triceratops peeking out from under the lifted top of the front egg

animations.description: something taps from inside the front egg: tap, tap, it gives two little hops in the nest, then sits still.
a bump jostles the nest: it rocks on its round bottom and the eggs rattle snugly in it, then everything settles.
a baby Triceratops hatches from the front egg, gives a big sleepy yawn and dozes off in its shell, its eggshell cap on its head.

pause.shows: a baby Triceratops fast asleep in its broken eggshell, its eggshell cap on its head
